Low. Receivables up 38 per cent and inventory up 41 per cent on sales up 11 means the reported profit is sitting in working capital rather than in the bank.

The position is weak behind an adequate-looking current ratio, the performance is a thin and thinning margin on growth the company cannot fund, and the test is whether the inventory can be converted to cash at book value in the next two quarters: if it can, the overdraft is a timing problem; if it cannot, a write-down at a 1.29 per cent net margin removes the whole of the year's profit.
